unresolved_candidates.reason: The proposed identity of Maacah daughter of Ouriel from Gabaon with Maacah daughter of Absalom is not established by these supplied-English units, despite the shared maternal connection to Abijah. The conflicting father descriptions remain unresolved. The retained regnal-summary comparison with 1 Kings 15:2 does not resolve this identity.

The prophecy is attributed to Adad in the source, whereas the chapter opens with the Spirit upon Azarias son of Oded. This review does not identify Adad with either Azarias or Oded or repair the attribution. The retained reform comparison does not depend on resolving the prophet's identity.

The source calls Asa's mother Maacah; Kings' regnal notice calls his mother Ana daughter of Absalom. Their personal identity is not resolved here. The retained comparison with the cult-removal narrative in 1 Kings 15:13 preserves its named woman, role, and objects without identifying the women independently.

semantic_findings: Retained narrative parallels preserve supplied names and variant numbers: 11:1 gives 180,000 versus 120,000; 13:2 gives three versus six regnal years and Ouriel versus Absalom parentage.

The Maacah/Ouriel/Absalom identity proposal, Adad/Azarias/Oded attribution proposal, and Maacah/Ana maternal identity proposal remain unresolved and receive zero pair and source completion credit. Narrative comparison at 15:16 preserves both named women, different roles, and idol versus hiding-place objects without resolving identity.

The 15:19/1 Kings 15:16 warfare summaries, 16:1 thirty-eighth-year date, and 16:13 thirty-ninth-year death date remain as supplied without harmonization. Pair 116 was corrected to distinguish the sleep wording from Kings burial-with-fathers wording.

City-list links at 11:6-10 connect named entries to the explicit fortification, provisioning, and armament summaries. Army-list links at 17:13,15-16,18-19 explain the explicit distinction between royal service and fortified-city forces. These are meaningful same-chapter literary links, not independent geographical or personal identification.

Military comparisons preserve their stated limits: shared equipment, specific ethnic force descriptions, or stated totals do not identify separate armies or campaigns. Victory-spoil and divine-terror comparisons preserve distinct enemies, geography, and chronology.
The 18:33 arrow comparison preserves accurate/good aim in both supplied texts; it does not import a random-shot description.

Author refinement 121 replaces an inferred explanation of the earlier-ways qualifier with the concrete instruction in 14:3. All eleven author refinement old/new complete triples were independently read and the final versions are supported.
limitations: Initial supplied-English AI curation; not exhaustive discovery, independent human scholarly review, original-language/apparatus verification, name-equivalence resolution, chronological harmonization, or live-anchor verification.
